title: Incremental token delta propagation for prefill hedging and decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Current prefill and prompt preprocessing paths perform full re-tokenization and normalization for many common request patterns (small edits, appended user context, templated prefixes). This causes unnecessary CPU work, delayed kernel selection, and KV-cache fragmentation which increases end-to-end latency for both prefill and early decode. We see this most acutely for low-latency single-turn requests where tokenization overhead dominates and for high-concurrency workloads where redundant work amplifies.

Goal: Implement an incremental tokenization and delta propagation mechanism on the prefill side that: (1) detects unchanged prefix segments and reuses tokenization artifacts (subtoken IDs, alignments, normalization mappings), (2) generates a compact delta bundle for only the changed suffix to allow fast kernel-selection and KV-cache reuse heuristics, and (3) integrates a speculative "hedged prefill" mode that surfaces a light-weight token footprint quickly to the scheduler so decode kernels can be provisioned earlier without waiting for full normalization.

Scope and design summary:
- Tokenization delta model: compute a deterministic fingerprint (hash+length) per canonical prefix segment boundary (sentence/segment heuristics). If fingerprint matches, reuse prior token id vector and normalization metadata. For changed suffixes compute an incremental token vector and a mapping that allows stitching with existing KV cache indices.
- Delta bundle format: small binary blob containing new token ids, alignment offsets, and a minimal provenance header (model-id, vocab-hash, normalization-version). Bundles should be versioned for forward compatibility.
- Prefill hedging: introduce a two-stage prefill path for latency-sensitive requests:
  - Stage 1 (hedge): run fast, approximate normalization + lightweight token hashing to provide token count and high-confidence kernel shape for early scheduling (<= 2ms target on x86 small instances).
  - Stage 2 (full): run full normalization/tokenization and produce the delta bundle. Stage 2 can be performed in parallel with early kernel allocation; stage 1 results direct the scheduler and batching decisions early.
- KV cache stitching: design an index translation layer so a reused prefix token vector maps to existing KV indices. For suffix deltas, apply an offset patch rather than full recomputation of KV offsets.
- Backward compatibility: bundles fall back to full tokenization if model/vocab/normalization version mismatch or if bundle is corrupted.

Implementation tasks:
- Token fingerprinting util (C++ runtime): deterministic, endian-safe hashes, segment boundary heuristics (ENG-99277-T1).
- Delta bundle serializer/deserializer (proto-lite) and versioning (ENG-99277-T2).
- Hedged prefill fast-normalizer (C++ + SIMD): ASCII fast-path with best-effort Unicode fallback (ENG-99277-T3).
- Scheduler integration: early kernel-selection hooks to accept Stage 1 signals (ENG-99277-T4).
- KV index translation and stitching logic (ENG-99277-T5).
- Unit + perf tests: microbenchmarks for single-turn latency, 95/99th latency under concurrency, and cost measurement (ENG-99277-T6).

Benchmarks & acceptance criteria:
- Hedged Stage 1 latency <= 2ms (p50) on a c6-standard-like CPU for 128-char average requests.
- End-to-end prefill overhead reduced by at least 25% p50 for single-turn templates with appended user context (measured on runtime-1.32 baseline).
- KV-cache reuse rate > 80% for repeated templated prefixes across a synthetic workload of 10k unique sessions.
- No regressions in tokenization correctness; all tokenization unit tests remain green and golden outputs identical when fallbacks trigger.

Rollout plan and safety:
1) Feature gated behind runtime flag profile=incr-token-delta and console toggle (canary to 5% traffic).
2) Start with internal dogfood and synthetic workloads; run for 48 hours and verify metrics (latency, CPU, KV reuse) vs control.
3) Enable hedged prefill for latency-critical customers only (documented in release notes). Monitor for increased downstream queuing or mis-scheduling.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: fingerprint collision or incorrect stitching causes bad KV alignment leading to decode corruption. Mitigation: include sanity checksums in delta bundle and conservative fallback to full tokenization on mismatch.
- Risk: hedged Stage 1 overspecifies kernel shape and causes inefficient kernels to be allocated. Mitigation: early signals are advisory to scheduler; allow scheduler to reconfigure if Stage 2 disagrees.
- Risk: added code complexity in token pipeline increases maintenance cost. Mitigation: keep delta serializer minimal, add comprehensive tests and telemetry for bundle format usage.

Observability & telemetry:
- Emit metrics: "delta_bundle_reused", "delta_bundle_fallback", "hedge_stage1_latency_ms", "kv_stitch_miss".
- Traces: attach bundle version and fingerprint to trace spans for tokenization-prefill.
- Dashboards: prefill overhead by customer tier and by request shape.

Documentation & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Incremental+Token+Delta+Propagation (draft)
- Proto definition PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proto/pull/245 (WIP)
- Scheduler hook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/889 (draft)

Acceptance criteria checklist (must pass before merge):
- [ ] Unit tests for bundle serializer + fingerprint util
- [ ] End-to-end perf run vs runtime-1.32 baseline
- [ ] Canary run on internal cluster with hedged prefill enabled
- [ ] Telemetry hooked and dashboard created
- [ ] Security review sign-off if any serialized bundle contains PII (N/A expected)
